data.one_liner: Flutter plugin to expose device-specific speech-to-text recognition capabilities.
data.what_it_does: Exposes device-specific speech recognition capabilities in Flutter. It allows capturing spoken words from the microphone and converting them to text via platform APIs.
use_when: You want to implement voice commands or short phrase recognition in your app.
You need cross-platform speech-to-text support across Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Web.
avoid_when: You need continuous spoken conversion or always-on listening.
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, macOS, Web, and Windows.
Provides callback handlers for results, status changes, and errors.
weaknesses: Android has a very short built-in pause timeout that cannot be customized.
Windows support is currently in beta and not yet fully production-ready.
data.setup_notes: Requires platform-specific permissions like microphone access and speech recognition descriptions in Info.plist (iOS/macOS) and AndroidManifest.xml (Android).
